summary: case-002 selection protocol preregistered (E1-E5 eligibility criteria, engine-blind row enumeration via direct visual inspection only, deterministic earliest-eligible-row tie-break) before the METI source was acquired or any row examined — a stronger preregistration discipline than case-001, which had no equivalent frozen protocol before selection.
Plain fetch()-based acquisition of the METI PDF failed: HTTP 202 with x-amzn-waf-action: challenge (AWS WAF Bot Control JS challenge) instead of the PDF.

Built scripts/source-acquisition/browser-fetch (Playwright/Chromium 1.63.0) to satisfy the WAF challenge by visiting the landing page in a real browser session first; successfully acquired and SHA-256-locked the METI PDF (106 pages, A4 landscape, Producer 'List Creator', not encrypted per pdfinfo). PDF magic bytes verified before locking.

Preregistered selection protocol applied via direct visual inspection (pdftoppm rendering, no compared engine used); target row frozen: PDF page index 8 (printed 経(本) 5), item 010 経済産業本省共通費, expense 01-95, the first 目-level expense-coded row in the document's detail table (明細表).

This page carries a printed (単位: 千円) unit label directly on the target page — a genuine structural difference from case-001's target page, noted at selection time as an observation, not a selection criterion.

Ground Truth frozen by direct visual inspection (400dpi pdftoppm renders, pixel-accurate crops), still before any engine was run. Delta observed as positive (4,556,824, no △ glyph), confirmed against six neighboring rows on the same page that do visibly carry △, ruling out a rendering artifact suppressing a faint glyph.

First frozen out-of-sample benchmark run against the unchanged, case-001-derived pipeline (no code changed after seeing this result). Scores: pdfjs-baseline 2/11, pymupdf-baseline 3/11, docling 2/11 — a severe regression from case-001's 8-9/11. Preserved permanently, never amended.

common.mjs's splitTrailingTriple requires the amount triple to be the literal end of the reconstructed line; case-002's annotation column (（要求要旨）) follows the triple on the SAME line, breaking triple extraction for both flat-text baselines — unlike case-001, where the equivalent annotation only ever appeared on continuation lines after the triple had already split off cleanly.

common.mjs lacks a CJK wrap-space-closing step that normalize-docling.mjs has; pdfjs-dist's letter-spacing artifact on this page's header row caused item_name_present_among_candidates to diverge between pdfjs (FAIL) and pymupdf (PASS), purely due to this asymmetry, unrelated to amounts or signs.

Docling's TableFormer produced a coarser, misaligned 23x12 grid for this page (vs. case-001's 21x14), merging multiple logical rows into single cells and splitting the target row's amount triple across grid rows; it confidently selected an unrelated, wrong row (itemCandidateCount: 1, no ambiguity flagged) rather than honestly failing.

H1 (Docling's table-cell separation generalizes across ministries): NOT SUPPORTED by this single contrasting case. H4 (unit-label recovery is page-context-dependent, not a fundamental extraction gap): SUPPORTED (unit_exact_match PASSed for all 3 engines here, unlike case-001). H6 (header-row hierarchy ambiguity persists): SUPPORTED for the flat-text engines; Docling's version manifested differently (a single wrongly-confident wrong-row match, not a flagged ambiguity).

evaluate.mjs's delta_glyph_observed_and_associated check hardcodes expected: 'contains △' regardless of Ground Truth, meaning no engine — however correct — could ever pass it for a document whose correct delta has no glyph, exactly case-002's own Ground Truth. Invisible with only case-001 (whose Ground Truth does have a glyph).

delta_glyph_observed_and_associated replaced with delta_sign_evidence_matches_source, which derives the expected glyph state from Ground Truth's own deltaRaw field instead of hardcoding it. Classified as evaluator overfit to case-001's specific source condition, not an extraction/normalization bug and not Ground Truth contamination (Ground Truth isolation was otherwise correct throughout).

case-002 re-scored under the corrected evaluator: pdfjs-baseline 3/11, pymupdf-baseline 4/11, docling 3/11 — exactly +1 per engine over the first frozen run (case002-e07), since no engine had ever fabricated a false glyph. Every other check's PASS/FAIL outcome was confirmed identical before and after. The original 2/11, 3/11, 2/11 result remains permanently preserved, not overwritten.

A single-fixture benchmark's checks can encode implicit assumptions from that fixture even when explicit Ground-Truth-isolation discipline is followed perfectly; checks themselves need to be re-examined against a second, independently-selected case before being trusted as fixture-independent. This is a distinct failure category from extraction/normalization bugs.

Whether splitTrailingTriple's trailing-anchor assumption can be relaxed to tolerate non-numeric trailing content (like this case's same-line annotation) without reintroducing amount-similarity-as-selection-evidence risk. Recommended as the single next follow-up experiment in both the first-frozen-run report and the evaluator-correction report.
Whether adding a closeCjkWrapSpaces-equivalent step to common.mjs/normalize.mjs fixes the item_name_present_among_candidates asymmetry found here without regressing case-001.

Why Docling's TableFormer produced a coarser, misaligned grid for this specific page, and whether an itemCandidateCount: 1 result should carry a lower-confidence signal when the winning cell's row position looks structurally inconsistent with neighboring cells.
Whether the annotation-on-same-line-as-triple pattern found here is common or rare across ministries — proposed as a reason for a future case-003, not executed by this backfill task.
